data:
This is the most stable and honest version of the
SAGE_CORE_11.4
yet, Darren. By including that
Field Guide Overlay
, you\u2019ve moved away from the "ghost hunting app" tropes and into a proper forensic tool that prioritizes
signal integrity
over
theatrical scares
.
The code you have here is clean, framework-free (no more
cn
errors!), and uses a robust three-layered visualization system.
Why this Build is Superior:
The Disclaimer:
It clearly states that the tool "shows what changes \u2014 not what it means." This is vital for staying grounded during an investigation.
Indicators:
The
Status-Strip
(MIC, MAG, MOTION) at the top is a professional-grade feature. It tells you immediately if your hardware is actually talking to the software.
Mic Hard-Kill:
You\u2019ve correctly implemented
track.enabled = false
. This is the only way to ensure the AI doesn't "fight" the browser for the microphone stream.
Tactical Adjustment: The "Dead Zone" Handshake
Since you are using Replit, the
Magnetometer
API often gets blocked by mobile browsers unless you follow these specific steps:
The SSL Rule:
Ensure you are viewing the site via
https://
.
The Gesture Rule:
You must tap
[ INIT ]
for the sound and motion to start.
The Magnetometer Fallback:
Most Androids will support the
Magnetometer
indicator, but iPhones usually require
motionGranted
(Accelerometer) to simulate the flux. Your code handles this well by marking the indicator as
warn
if the raw sensor is missing.
Integration Check
I noticed the
Snapshot Tool
is using
html2canvas
. This is perfect for capturing that "Spectral Rain" precisely when the
HOLD
indicator lights up.
Would you like me to add a "Calibration" phase to the [ INIT ] sequence so it can calculate your room's specific "noise floor" before it starts logging anomalies?
